_what: What a person handed over for a course, filed by a session (S693, 2026-11-20). `entries` are pasted course data from the hand-over box (commons_handover, kind paste): the catalog description and the units or hours as the person typed them, with where they found it. `notes` are a person's findings that are no data (kind note, or said in session before the box took notes). A person's entry wins over a later machine read of the same course: a reader that holds both keeps this one. Readers: the M-ID description pipeline (an M-ID card with no description) and the no-longer-offered check, which reads `not_in_catalog` as its catalog factor and sets nothing aside on it alone (r-no-longer-offered-sam-2026-11-20). Join on control_number, which a re-mint never changes; mid_card_at_filing is a stored id (resolve it through kb/alias_chain.py before comparing it to the live set).
source: commons_handover rows, read live 2026-11-20 by S693 (`handover` is the row id's first eight characters); the four notes are Sam's words in session the same day, before the box took notes: "I got to Ohlone's BRDC 127A, 127B, 127C and 127D and they are not in the catalog, but there is no place for me to note that."
catalog_row_note: `catalog_row` names the same course in the catalog rows the runner filed (kb/hand_filed_catalogs/courses/<slug>.json.gz). `description_agrees` is true when the two descriptions open with the same words for at least nine tenths of the shorter one (`same_opening_characters`, whitespace and case set aside); a person's paste often carries the requisite and offering lines the runner's row files apart. None is filed for Grossmont.
machine_check_of_notes: Not run. The session's network does not reach www.ohlone.edu; the runner's page read (college-page-read.yml) can read the chapter. Until it does, the four notes rest on Sam's reading of chapter 7 of the 2026-2027 catalog.

entries.title: Staying Mentally Sharp for OA
entries.description: This course provides older adults with the tools to reach their optimum levels of brainpower through skill-building with memory techniques. Also covered are decision-making, problem-solving, planning, and determining opportunities for cognitive growth.

entries.title: Parenting Adult/Children W/Dis
entries.description: A class designed to provide support and resources to parents who have an adult child with a disability. Guest speakers will be invited to present information to help parents be knowledgeable of what their community offers in regards to independence.

entries.title: Orthopedic Anatomy and Physiology
entries.description:
A study of the development of the muscular-skeletal systems with the emphasis on gross anatomy of the bones, arterial and venous perfusion, and relevant nervous innervation as they relate to the treatment of orthopedic injuries. (CSU)
Prerequisite: Admission to the Orthopedic Technology Program.  
Corequisite: Concurrent enrollment in OT 111 and OT 112.

entries.title: BUILDING CODES II
entries.description:
Continuation of CI 60. Presents an enforcement perspective and continues the interpretation and application of the International Building Code (IBC). (Students may repeat this course no more than twice in a six-year period.) [D]
Grade Only
Offered: SPRING

entries.title: MICROCOMPUTER REPAIR AND SERVICE
entries.description: Provides instruction on microcomputer maintenance and service. Includes training in safety, hardware, software, computer assembly, customer relations, testing, troubleshooting, and replacing computer components. Includes operating system, applications, command line for technicians, and software diagnostics. [D] (Same as: ELEC 10A)

entries.title: CENTRAL SERVICE TECHNOLOGY
entries.description: Introduces basic functions of a Central Service Department and includes microbiology, aseptic technique, disinfecting equipment, decontamination and sterilization as well as wrapping and packaging of surgical instruments. Provides a review of body systems and identification of instruments used in surgery. Emphasizes medical terminology, safety precautions, risk management, regulations, inventory management, ethical responsibilities, and communication skills. [D] Offered: Fall
